title: What Is Conformance Testing? Definition & Examples
snippet: API conformance testing verifies that a live API's behavior — response schemas, status codes, headers, and error formats — matches its declared specification, such as an OpenAPI document. API conformance testing is a complement to API contract testing, but more expansive: it tests not only the technical contract but also the business rules that need to be enforced by the API in context.

title: ETSI - ETSI Blog - Insights on API conformance testing for NFV-MANO APIs
snippet: ETSI GS NFV-TST 010 is a published API conformance testing specification for NFV Management and Orchestration APIs. The latest released version is Version 2.6.1, which aligns with the corresponding versions of the SOL documents for reference point specifications.

title: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
snippet: RFC 9457 defines simple JSON and XML document formats to describe the specifics of a problem encountered -- problem details. RFC 9457 Problem Details is an IETF standard that defines a consistent, machine-readable JSON format for HTTP API error responses with standard fields for type, title, status, detail, and instance.

title: Authentication and Authorization in APIs
snippet: API gateway authentication verifies client identity at a centralized entry point before requests reach backend services. Common authentication methods include OAuth 2.0, JWT, API keys, or mutual TLS (mTLS). API gateways enforce RBAC and ABAC policies, offering advantages like centralized security management, reduced backend development workload, enhanced security, and improved scalability and flexibility.

title: API gateway security: 8 best practices
snippet: The API gateway acts as a centralized entry point for managing and securing access to APIs. API gateways serve as the entry point for API requests, handling authentication and authorization uniformly. Centralized enforcement reduces duplicated authentication logic and creates one control point for access policies.
